title: The Mathematical Modeling Software Signature Database — Overview: Signature mathematics workbenches
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature mathematics workbenches are original modeling environments designed in the Signature system: one for exact symbolic work, one for fast numeric arrays, one for honest statistics. Each workbench follows the Signature doctrine — the tool explains its own answers, shows its working, and never hides uncertainty. These are original designs, labeled as such, with working demonstrations of their core ideas.
capabilities: Three original workbenches: symbolic, numeric, statistical
Doctrine: explain answers, show working, never hide uncertainty

title: The Mathematical Modeling Software Signature Database — Signature symbolic workbench
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature symbolic workbench manipulates mathematics exactly: expressions are trees, and every transformation — expand, factor, differentiate — is a tree rewrite the user can inspect step by step. Nothing is approximated silently; when the workbench must go numeric it says so and names the method. The demo differentiates a polynomial term by term, the way the workbench rewrites expression trees.
capabilities: No silent approximation: numeric steps are announced

title: The Mathematical Modeling Software Signature Database — Signature numeric workbench
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature numeric workbench treats arrays as first-class citizens and iteration as the honest engine: every loop shows its convergence, every solver reports its residual. The workbench refuses to return an answer without an error estimate — a number without uncertainty is a rumor. The demo runs Newton's method with the residual printed at each step, the way the workbench insists.
capabilities: No answer without an error estimate

title: The Mathematical Modeling Software Signature Database — Signature statistical workbench
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature statistical workbench practices honest statistics: every summary carries its sample size, every comparison carries its uncertainty, and the workbench warns loudly when data are too few to support a conclusion. P-hacking guards are built in — the workbench counts how many questions were asked of the data and discounts accordingly. The demo computes a confidence interval the workbench way: estimate, interval, and sample size together.
capabilities: Every summary carries its sample size

title: The Mathematical Modeling Software Signature Database — Signature modeling language
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature modeling language lets a model be written the way it is thought: declare the unknowns, write the equations, name what to solve for. The language separates the model (timeless equations) from the experiment (which parameters, which solver, which outputs), so one model serves many experiments. The demo parses a tiny model declaration into equations and unknowns.
capabilities: Models written the way they are thought

demo.title: Model declaration parse
demo.code: function parseModel(src){const eqs=src.split(';').map(s=>s.trim()).filter(Boolean);const unknowns=[...new Set(eqs.join(' ').match(/[a-z]+/g))].filter(v=>!['sin','cos','exp'].includes(v));return {equations:eqs.length,unknowns};}const m=parseModel('x + y = 5; x - y = 1');J(m);assert(m.equations===2&&m.unknowns.join(',')==='x,y','modellang');

title: The Mathematical Modeling Software Signature Database — Signature solver doctrine
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature solver doctrine ranks methods by honesty: direct methods that finish, iterative methods that report, and heuristic methods that confess they might be wrong. The doctrine's rule is that the solver must be matched to the problem's manners — stiff equations get implicit methods, noisy data gets robust ones — and the mismatch log is a required output. A solver applied blindly is a gamble; the doctrine replaces gambling with matchmaking.
capabilities: Solvers ranked by honesty: direct, iterative, heuristic
Match the solver to the problem's manners

title: The Mathematical Modeling Software Signature Database — Signature plotting doctrine
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature plotting doctrine holds that a plot is an argument: every figure must have a claim in its title, labeled axes with units, and no truncated axes that exaggerate. The workbench's plots annotate the interesting point — the maximum, the crossing, the anomaly — instead of leaving the reader to hunt. The demo builds a plot specification object the way the doctrine requires: claim, axes, units, annotations.
capabilities: Every plot is an argument with a claim

demo.title: Plot specification builder
demo.code: function plotSpec(claim,x,xUnit,y,yUnit,notes){return {claim,x:{label:x,unit:xUnit},y:{label:y,unit:yUnit},annotations:notes,ok:!!(claim&&xUnit&&yUnit)};}const p=plotSpec('drag rises with speed','velocity','m/s','drag','N',['peak at 60 m/s']);J({ok:p.ok,claim:p.claim});assert(p.ok===true,'plotspec');

title: The Mathematical Modeling Software Signature Database — Signature verification doctrine for models
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature model verification doctrine proves models the way testing proves code: unit checks on each equation, integration checks on coupled systems, and validation against measured data with the error published. A model that has never met data is labeled untested, however beautiful. The doctrine's final gate is the prediction log — the model writes down what it expects before the experiment runs, and the database keeps score.
capabilities: Equation unit checks and system integration checks
Validation against measured data, errors published
Untested label for models that never met data
